text: Wall Street just had a brutal day. The Dow lost more than eleven hundred points.
The S&P 500 fell two percent. Its sixth straight loss, and now eight percent below its record.
Domino one: rates. Markets expect the Fed to hike again in December, and higher rates hit stock values.
Domino two: AI doubts. Nvidia lost its CEO, and a short seller hit AMD.
Domino three: even the biggest IPO ever couldn't fix the mood. Anthropic opened up thirty-four percent, and closed up seventeen.
Now, perspective. Since 1980, the S&P 500 has dropped about fourteen percent at some point in an average year. And still finished higher in roughly three out of four years.
Eight percent off the top hurts. It is not unusual.
Your call: is this panic, or profit? Comment PANIC or PROFIT.
